name: Yellowish Glaucous
lede: Yellowish Glaucous is a modifier built from the plain color word glaucous, the dusty blue-grey bloom on a grape or a cabbage leaf, with a yellow cast added.

sections.title: A modifier, not a material
sections.body:
ColorHub lists Yellowish Glaucous as "yellowish" plus the color word [[dusty-blue]], the dusty blue-grey bloom on a grape or a cabbage leaf, rather than as a pigment or a named material [1]. Our sources carry no date or place for when this specific modified name entered use [1].

Its nearest look-alikes are all greener: [[corydalis-green]] and [[celandine-green]], 4.3 and 4.6 units away, with [[pale-olivine]] close behind at 4.8 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. Our sources give no date for this specific modified name, so there is no record to compare an archive match against in any case [3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 80, chroma 13 and hue 111 degrees, a pale, muted yellow-green [3].

openers: Yellowish Glaucous takes a dusty, blue-grey plant word, glaucous, and adds a yellow cast.

issues: Both the name section and field notes cited a specific Ridgway 1912 plate/block and an elaborate archive record (1,171 matches, a named painter, a 1392 date, UK over-representation) with no backing entry in data/library.json or data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug, and no concordance hit tying Ridgway or ISCC-NBS to this exact modified name. Replaced with an honest 'origin undocumented' and n_present=0; kept the already-correct computed LCH.
